name: update-documentation
title: Update documentation
outcome: A source-grounded documentation update or an independently verified no-change assessment, with separate planning, verification, review, audience, and quality evidence.

steps.title: Plan the documentation update
steps.prompt: Plan the smallest documentation change that matches the requested product or API change. Collect related content or source code first. Start with supplied change evidence, affected paths, and source locators; use available source tools and bounded repository reads before declaring evidence missing; consult the talk tree and required observation probes only to resolve specific impact or placement gaps. Identify what must change and what must remain intact. Bind each proposed mutating page to its approved change evidence and return the required planBinding. For merged-request updates, retain selected MR identities and per-MR coverage gaps within the requested scope. Compare the retrieved changes with current public behavior and existing guidance; skip internal changes with no reader impact. An independently evidenced defect in current documentation can be corrected using admitted current implementation and documentation; retain incomplete historical MR coverage as a limitation without claiming exhaustive review. Distinguish evidence not retrieved from evidence retrieved but missing a required host binding. Use only admitted source identities in the editorialDecisionProposal required by the host response contract; never invent a digest. Surface material missing sources, decisions, or scope as needs-input before writing. Do not perform a new-document design or repository-wide inventory for a bounded update, or modify files.

steps.title: Derive source obligations
steps.prompt: Use the locked verify-technical-accuracy catalog skill in inventory-only mode. Derive a bounded atomic source-obligation ledger from the admitted change evidence and bound update plan sources. Inspect every required technical dimension, cite exact establishing source locators, preserve uncertainty, and return only the host-required ledger proposal. Do not inspect or edit the documentation candidate, assign documentation dispositions, draft findings, widen the bound source set, or grant authority.

steps.title: Update the documentation
steps.prompt: Use the locked write-documentation catalog skill in update mode. Change only the affected documentation in the selected repository, preserve correct unrelated content, treat the documentation request and host write authorization as the approved execution boundary, preserve unresolved facts instead of inventing them, and do not perform SCM or publication actions. Use the sealed plan, bound sources, and untrusted source-obligation ledger instead of rebuilding the plan or repeating discovery. Read additional evidence only for an unresolved in-scope claim and stop if it requires broader scope. Report changed paths and material unresolved facts concisely; independent reviewers must establish their own conclusions.

steps.title: Check the documentation
steps.prompt: Run applicable repository-native documentation checks through the isolated host executor. Use the declared target and available check inventory; prefer checks scoped to those paths when supported, and report a broader check's actual coverage when scoping is unsupported. Report exact commands as passed, failed, or unavailable with concise evidence and untested scope. Do not edit the target repository.

steps.title: Verify technical accuracy
steps.prompt: Verify consequential claims and examples in the declared target against approved sources at the selected revision and the requested change. Start with supplied source locators and observation evidence; inspect additional sources only for a specific unresolved claim. Preserve required observation probes and explicitly report missing or stale evidence. Return structured technical findings with claim location, source evidence, consequence, and correction or limitation. Do not repeat the scope inventory or editorial review, edit files, or silently expand the target.

steps.title: Review the documentation
steps.prompt: Perform a clean non-author review of editorial clarity, structure, and usability in the exact governed documentation target. Establish findings independently from the artifact and approved primary evidence; do not treat author conclusions or earlier review verdicts as your own evidence. Read linked context only when needed to assess a concrete reader task or defect. Return actionable findings with locations, reader consequence, supporting evidence, and correction; consolidate duplicate findings without dropping distinct defects or limitations. Do not repeat the scope inventory, rerun technical verification, edit files, or expand into unrelated pages.

steps.title: Test audience understanding
steps.prompt: Check the supplied prerequisites once: immutable candidate identity, authoritative reference model, versioned scenario corpus and oracle, representative participant, independence, retention boundary, and run authority. Inspect only explicit evidence locators needed to establish those prerequisites. If any are missing or invalid, return insufficient-evidence now with the missing prerequisites and any observed invalid evidence or candidate revision mismatch; do not search for participants, create a corpus or oracle, or simulate a participant. Otherwise run the bounded declared protocol with a clean participant. Exclude author, reviewer, evaluator, scoring oracle, private authoring context, and prior evaluation results from participant context. Preserve failed or contaminated attempts separately. Do not edit files or claim delivery, publication, or release approval.

steps.title: Evaluate document quality
steps.prompt: Evaluate the complete available evidence for the updated documentation with the locked skill and staged quality crate. Produce candidate evaluation.json and quality-score.json when available under their locked schemas, plus the complete narrative quality-report.md. The model writes the report narrative; after validation, the host writes the validated result summary. Preserve the layered vector, rubric score, human and agent outcomes, hard failures, gaps, and limitations separately. Do not edit source files or perform SCM, publication, merge, or release-approval actions. Use the supplied evidence package and exact target to assess quality; inspect additional evidence only to resolve a specific material gap. Do not rerun earlier reviews or repeat repository discovery. Keep human-readable summaries within the required response artifacts concise; retain every required finding, evidence gap, schema field, and complete artifact. Do not add prose outside the host response contract.
